skill.name: uml-modeling
skill.description: Design, critique, and revise UML diagrams with clear modeling principles, boundaries, and diagram selection rules.
skill.summary: Create and improve UML diagrams that communicate software structure, behavior, interactions, and deployment clearly.
skill.author: Carbocode

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown backticks and UML guidance words as risky patterns. Reviewed context shows documentation-only guidance, no executable commands, network access, data exfiltration, or prompt injection. All static findings are assessed as false positives.

content.value_statement: UML diagrams often become confusing when they mix structure, behavior, lifecycle, and deployment concerns. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose the right UML form and improve diagram clarity.
actual_capabilities: Selects between class, object, package, component, deployment, use case, activity, state machine, and interaction diagrams.
Reviews UML for semantic errors, unclear boundaries, abstraction drift, and wrong diagram type.
Uses bundled reference files and per-diagram deep dives before applying notation.
Guides self-contained diagrams that explain scope, actors, external systems, and constraints.
Helps split broad modeling questions into separate UML diagrams when needed.
limitations: It does not render images by itself; output depends on the requested notation or host tool.
It cannot infer domain facts that are absent from the prompt or repository.
It focuses on UML modeling, not general charting or decorative visuals.
It may ask for clarification when the modeling boundary is ambiguous.

use_cases.title: Architecture Reviews
use_cases.description: Review diagrams for component boundaries, runtime topology, dependencies, and whether the chosen UML form answers the question.

use_cases.title: Developer Documentation
use_cases.description: Create self-contained diagrams that explain domain structure, workflows, states, and service interactions for maintainers.

use_cases.title: Product Scope Modeling
use_cases.description: Create use case or activity models that clarify user goals, system boundaries, and workflow decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Diagram Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request without a chosen UML form
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best UML diagram type for this feature. Explain the choice, then create a self-contained diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Workflow Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a UML activity diagram for this process. Include boundaries, roles, decisions, guards, and important data objects.

prompt_templates.title: Review An Existing Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UML diagram for semantic errors, wrong diagram type, unclear boundaries, and notation choices that may confuse readers.

prompt_templates.title: Split A Complex System View
prompt_templates.prompt: Model this system with the smallest useful set of UML diagrams. Separate structure, lifecycle, interaction, and deployment concerns.

output_examples.input: A team asks for one diagram showing classes, deployment, and request flow.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends separate class, deployment, and sequence diagrams. It explains each purpose and avoids mixing incompatible UML grammars.

output_examples.input: A state diagram uses actions such as validate request as states.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the semantic error and proposes persistent states, event triggers, guards, and transition effects.

output_examples.input: A user requests a diagram but does not know which UML type to use.
output_examples.output: The skill infers the modeling question, selects the UML form, and asks only for facts needed to complete the model.

best_practices: Start with the modeling question before choosing notation or layout.
Keep one abstraction level and one main purpose in each diagram.
Make boundaries, actors, external systems, and constraints explicit.
anti_patterns: Do not combine class, sequence, state, and deployment concerns in one diagram.
Do not use use case diagrams for screens, buttons, or internal functions.
Do not polish layout before fixing the diagram type or semantics.

faq.question: Can this skill choose the UML diagram type?
faq.answer: Yes. It infers the best UML form from the modeling goal and the available context.

faq.question: Can it review diagrams I already have?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks semantics, boundaries, abstraction level, self-containment, and readability.

faq.question: Does it generate PlantUML or Mermaid?
faq.answer: It can guide textual diagram output when requested, but it focuses first on modeling correctness.

faq.question: Which UML diagram types are covered?
faq.answer: It covers structure, behavior, interaction, deployment, use case, state machine, activity, sequence, and related diagrams.

faq.question: Is it only for software architects?
faq.answer: No. Engineers, writers, analysts, testers, and product teams can use it for clearer system explanations.

faq.question: Does the skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains Markdown guidance and reference files for UML modeling.
